title: Getting around
goal: Ask for and understand directions, take a bus, train or auto-rickshaw, and give instructions politely or informally.
intro: Odia towns are organised around **ଛକ** (*chhôkô*) — junctions or squares that serve as landmarks (Master Canteen Chhak, Rasulgarh Chhak…). In this unit you learn the three levels of **command** (formal, familiar, intimate) and the endings for movement: **-କୁ** 'to', **-ରୁ** 'from'.

vocab.en: to get on, board; to climb

phrases.en: Excuse me, where is the station?
phrases.note: ଶୁଣନ୍ତୁ 'listen' is the polite way to get attention.

phrases.en: How far is it from here?

phrases.native: ବେଶି ଦୂର ନୁହେଁ, ପାଞ୍ଚ ମିନିଟ୍ ବାଟ।
phrases.roman: besi durô nuheṃ, pañchô miniṭ baṭô.

phrases.en: Does this bus go to Puri?
Will you go to Lingaraj Temple? (to a driver)
How much will the fare be?
Where can I get a ticket?

grammar.title: Commands at three levels
grammar.body:
The imperative matches the three levels of 'you':

**Formal (ଆପଣ)**: stem + **-ଅନ୍ତୁ** — କରନ୍ତୁ, ଯାଆନ୍ତୁ, ଆସନ୍ତୁ, ବସନ୍ତୁ, ଦିଅନ୍ତୁ, ନିଅନ୍ତୁ, କୁହନ୍ତୁ, ରୁହନ୍ତୁ
**Familiar (ତୁମେ)**: stem + **-ଅ** — କର, ଯାଅ, ଆସ, ବସ, ଦିଅ, ନିଅ, କୁହ, ରୁହ
**Intimate (ତୁ)**: bare stem — କର୍, ଯା, ଆ, ବସ୍, ଦେ, ନେ, କହ, ରହ

To say **don't**, add ନାହିଁ (ଡେରି କରନ୍ତୁ ନାହିଁ) or, more gently, use the future + ନାହିଁ (ଡେରି କରିବେ ନାହିଁ). A polite request can also be a future question: ଏଠି ରଖିବେ? 'Will you stop here?'. With strangers like drivers and shopkeepers, formal forms are safest, though many people use ତୁମେ with drivers younger than them.

grammar.title: Movement: -କୁ (to), -ରୁ (from), -ରେ (by), ଯାଏ (up to)
grammar.body:
**-କୁ** marks the destination: ମନ୍ଦିରକୁ 'to the temple'. With ଯିବା and place names, -କୁ is often dropped: କଟକ ଯିବି 'I'll go to Cuttack'.
**-ରୁ** marks the starting point: ଷ୍ଟେସନରୁ 'from the station', ଏଠାରୁ 'from here'.
**-ରେ** also means 'by (vehicle)': ବସରେ 'by bus', ଟ୍ରେନରେ 'by train'.
**ଯାଏ** or **ପର୍ଯ୍ୟନ୍ତ** after a noun means 'up to, as far as': ଛକ ଯାଏ.

A useful pattern for directions is the **-ଇ** participle ('having done'): ସିଧା **ଯାଇ** ବାଁକୁ ବୁଲନ୍ତୁ 'go straight and (then) turn left'.

examples.en: He/She is coming from the station.
Walk as far as the junction.
How far is the market from here?

dialogue.title: To the Lingaraj Temple
dialogue.setting: Sam asks a passer-by the way, then bargains with an auto-rickshaw driver in Old Town, Bhubaneswar.

lines.speaker: Sam
lines.en: Excuse me, where is the Lingaraj Temple?

lines.speaker: Passer-by
lines.native: ଏଠାରୁ ଟିକେ ଦୂର। ସିଧା ଯାଇ ଦ୍ୱିତୀୟ ଛକରୁ ବାଁ ପଟକୁ ବୁଲନ୍ତୁ।
lines.roman: eṭharu ṭike durô. sidha jai dwitiyô chhôkôru baṃ pôṭôku bulôntu.
lines.en: It's a bit far from here. Go straight and turn left at the second junction.

lines.speaker: Passer-by
lines.native: ହଁ, କିନ୍ତୁ କୋଡ଼ିଏ ମିନିଟ୍ ଲାଗିବ। ଅଟୋରେ ଯାଆନ୍ତୁ।
lines.roman: hôṃ, kintu koṛie miniṭ lagibô. ôṭore jaôntu.
lines.en: Yes, but it'll take twenty minutes. Take an auto.

lines.speaker: Sam
lines.en: Brother, will you go to Lingaraj Temple?

lines.speaker: Sam
lines.en: Fine. Drop me in front of the temple, please.

culture: Directions in Odisha are given by landmarks — a *chhak*, a temple, a well-known shop — rather than street names. Agree on the fare before getting into an auto-rickshaw, or use app-based autos in Bhubaneswar and Cuttack. Address drivers and strangers as **ଭାଇ** (brother), **ଭାଇନା** or **ଅପା**. Note that non-Hindus are not allowed inside the Jagannath Temple in Puri or the Lingaraj Temple, though both can be viewed from outside.
